From 4007844b05815717f522c7ea9914e24ad0ff6c79 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2020 11:31:35 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] soc: mediatek: Check if power domains can be powered on at
 boot time

In the error case, where a power domain cannot be powered on
successfully at boot time (in mtk_register_power_domains),
pm_genpd_init would still be called with is_off=false, and the
system would later try to disable the power domain again, triggering
warnings as disabled clocks are disabled again (and other potential
issues).

Also print a warning splat in that case, as this should never
happen.

Fixes: c84e358718a66f7 ("soc: Mediatek: Add SCPSYS power domain driver")
Signed-off-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200928113107.v2.1.I5e6f8c262031d0451fe7241b744f4f3111c1ce71@changeid
Signed-off-by: Matthias Brugger <matthias.bgg@gmail.com>

diff --git a/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c b/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c
index f669d3754627..ca75b14931ec 100644
--- a/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c
+++ b/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c
@@ -524,6 +524,7 @@ static void mtk_register_power_domains(struct platform_device *pdev,
 	for (i = 0; i < num; i++) {
 		struct scp_domain *scpd = &scp->domains[i];
 		struct generic_pm_domain *genpd = &scpd->genpd;
+		bool on;
 
 		/*
 		 * Initially turn on all domains to make the domains usable
@@ -531,9 +532,9 @@ static void mtk_register_power_domains(struct platform_device *pdev,
 		 * software.  The unused domains will be switched off during
 		 * late_init time.
 		 */
-		genpd->power_on(genpd);
+		on = !WARN_ON(genpd->power_on(genpd) < 0);
 
-		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false);
+		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, !on);
 	}
 
 	/*
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c`**
   - A new boolean variable `on` is introduced to track the success of powering on the power domains.
   - The call to `genpd->power_on(genpd)` is modified to check for errors using `WARN_ON`, which will now set `on` to `false` if the power on operation fails (i.e., returns a negative value).
   - The `pm_genpd_init` function call is updated to use the value of `on` to determine whether to initialize the power domain as off or on. If `on` is `false`, it initializes the power domain as off.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in the `mtk-scpsys.c` file are directly related to improving error handling during the power domain initialization process. By introducing the `on` variable, the patch ensures that if a power domain fails to power on, it will not incorrectly initialize the power domain as on, which could lead to subsequent errors and warnings when the system attempts to disable it. This change enhances the robustness of the power management system by preventing potential issues that arise from mismanagement of power states during boot time.

Here is the commit message:
soc: mediatek: Check if power domains can be powered on at
 boot time

In the error case, where a power domain cannot be powered on
successfully at boot time (in mtk_register_power_domains),
pm_genpd_init would still be called with is_off=false, and the
system would later try to disable the power domain again, triggering
warnings as disabled clocks are disabled again (and other potential
issues).

Also print a warning splat in that case, as this should never
happen.

Fixes: c84e358718a66f7 ("soc: Mediatek: Add SCPSYS power domain driver")
Signed-off-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200928113107.v2.1.I5e6f8c262031d0451fe7241b744f4f3111c1ce71@changeid
Signed-off-by: Matthias Brugger <matthias.bgg@gmail.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the `pm_genpd_init` function is called with `is_off=false` even when the power domain fails to power on successfully. This leads to the system attempting to disable a power domain that was never properly enabled, resulting in warnings and potential issues with disabled clocks being disabled again.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void mtk_register_power_domains(struct platform_device *pdev,
 				struct scp *scp, int num)
 {
 	struct genpd_onecell_data *pd_data;
 	int i, ret;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < num; i++) {
 		struct scp_domain *scpd = &scp->domains[i];
 		struct generic_pm_domain *genpd = &scpd->genpd;
+		bool on;
 
 		/*
 		 * Initially turn on all domains to make the domains usable
 		 * with !CONFIG_PM and to get the hardware in sync with the
 		 * software.  The unused domains will be switched off during
 		 * late_init time.
 		 */
-		genpd->power_on(genpd);
+		on = !WARN_ON(genpd->power_on(genpd) < 0);
 
-		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false);
+		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, !on);
 	}
 
 	/*
 	 * We are not allowed to fail here since there is no way to unregister
 	 * a power domain. Once registered above we have to keep the domains
 	 * valid.
 	 */
 
 	pd_data = &scp->pd_data;
 
 	ret = of_genpd_add_provider_onecell(pdev->dev.of_node, pd_data);
 	if (ret)
 		dev_err(&pdev->dev, "Failed to add OF provider: %d\n", ret);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false);
genpd->power_on(genpd);
```
Reason:
The `pm_genpd_init` function is called with `is_off=false` regardless of whether the power domain was successfully powered on. If `genpd->power_on(genpd)` fails (returns a negative value), the power domain is still initialized as if it were on, leading to attempts to disable a domain that was never properly enabled, causing warnings and potential issues.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
on = !WARN_ON(genpd->power_on(genpd) < 0);
pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, !on);
```
Reason:
The patch checks the return value of `genpd->power_on(genpd)` and sets the `on` variable accordingly. If the power on fails, `on` will be false, and `pm_genpd_init` will be called with `is_off=true`, preventing the system from trying to disable a power domain that was not successfully enabled, thus avoiding warnings and potential issues.
